headline: Yandex bot traffic plummets after Ukraine drone strikes cripple data centers
summary: Bot traffic from Russia's largest tech company has dropped to near zero following targeted drone attacks on its key data centers. Services are reporting widespread outages.
details: Ukraine has effectively neutralized Russian bot traffic by striking Yandex's major data centers. Cloudflare reports that bot traffic from the Yandex network has fallen to just 0.4% of its previous levels.
The attacks targeted Yandex's largest data centers, including facilities in Sasovo and Kaluga. These strikes are reportedly a response to Russia's own attacks on Ukrainian data centers.

Yandex, often referred to as Russia's Google, is experiencing significant disruptions. At least 84 services are offline, with network traffic for Yandex Cloud and Yandex LLC dropping dramatically, impacting millions of users.

This escalation in cyber and drone warfare highlights the evolving tactics in the ongoing conflict. The strikes on data centers, previously considered less conventional targets, demonstrate a new phase of the hostilities.
The disruption to Yandex services means ordinary Russians have limited access to online services, with no viable high-speed satellite internet alternatives available within Russia.

topic: open source ai encourages outdoor activity
headline_marked: [[TouchGrass AI]] turns screen time into small outdoor adventures
headline: TouchGrass AI turns screen time into small outdoor adventures
summary: An open-source web app uses AI to generate personalized outdoor quests, encouraging users to spend less time on screens and more time outside.
details: A new open-source project called TouchGrass AI aims to combat excessive screen time by encouraging users to engage in outdoor activities. The web application generates personalized outdoor quests based on user preferences for time available, activity type, difficulty, and group size.

The goal is to make outdoor excursions more accessible and enjoyable, even for those with limited time. The hosted demo offers pre-set quests, allowing users to experience the app without needing to install any AI models locally.

While the hosted version uses fallback quests, the application is designed to leverage local AI generation using models like Qwen2.5 0.5B via Ollama. This allows users to run quest generation on their own computers, enhancing privacy and reducing reliance on third-party AI services.

Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python, TouchGrass is open-source under the MIT License. The project serves as an early prototype demonstrating how accessible AI tools and open-source software can transform an idea into a usable application.

The developer highlights the learning experience gained from integrating frontend, backend, local AI models, response validation, and fallback logic. This project emphasizes the power of open innovation in allowing developers to experiment and build useful tools.
